title: Cap. II Arg. 3: 1 Cor. 2:9 — prepared for those who love him (king/crown analogy)
pass_a_gloss: Thirdly, that place is brought from 1 Cor. ii. 9. Eye hath not seen, &c. the things which God hath prepared for them that love him. Those words, for them that love him, according to the common manner of speaking, indicate the very cause of the preparation. For if one should say that a King had prepared or destined a crown for those ascending the walls of some city under assault, by that saying he would signify that from foresight of the ascent this crown was destined to this or that man, and not otherwise.
pass_b_english: Third: they bring 1 Cor. 2:9 — "Eye has not seen… the things God prepared for those who love him." On ordinary speech, "for those who love him" looks like the cause of the preparation. Say a king prepared a crown for whoever scales a besieged city's walls: that would mean the crown was destined to this or that man from foresight of the climb — and no other way.
source_text: Tertio, affertur illud ex 1. Cor. ii. 9. Oculus non vidit, &c. quae praeparavit Deus iis qui diligunt illum. Verba illa, iis qui diligunt illum, secundum communem loquendi modum ipsam causam praeparationis indicant. Nam si quis diceret Regem praeparasse aut destinasse coronam adscendentibus muros oppugnatae alicujus civitatis, hoc dicto significaret ex praevisione adscensionis hanc coronam esse huic vel illi destinatam, & non aliter.
